laws.rule: Since 17 September 2023 the default speed limit on restricted roads in Wales (generally built-up roads with street lights) is 20 mph, not 30 mph; some roads keep 30 mph by local order and are signed.
laws.heading: Restricted Roads (20 mph Speed Limit) (Wales) Order 2022

laws.rule: Under the Visitor Accommodation (Register and Levy) Etc. (Wales) Act 2025, councils that choose to can charge a visitor levy of GBP 1.30 per person per night (about A$2.47, RBA rate of 30 October 2026), or 75p (about A$1.43) in hostels, bunkhouses and on tent pitches, from 1 April 2027 at the earliest. Cardiff is the first council confirmed to start, on 1 April 2027.
laws.heading: Visitor Accommodation (Register and Levy) Etc. (Wales) Act 2025

laws.rule: Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park: wild camping is not permitted anywhere in the park without the landowner's or farmer's permission, and the park authority owns little land and cannot give that consent. Camping in car parks or on roadside verges is not allowed at any time, and the park says overnight stays in a campervan or caravan in a car park are not permitted. The authority recommends official campsites and booking early. Its wild camping code asks for one night only and no fires or disposable barbecues. The pages name no penalty.

Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park: most of the park is privately owned, so lighting a barbecue or fire needs the landowner's permission. Some campsites allow gas stoves, barbecues or fires. The authority asks people to avoid open fires and barbecues where they can, because they are a main cause of wildfire.

Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon): the park authority says to use the official car parks for the walks, not lay-bys on the road up to Pen y Pass, and not to park in residential areas of the small communities near the car parks. It runs the Sherpa'r Wyddfa bus to Pen y Pass. The page gives no fee or penalty figures.

Wales sets a minimum price for alcohol: 65p per unit of alcohol (about A$1.24 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = GBP 0.5258), from 1 October 2026 (it was 50p before). It is an offence for an alcohol retailer to supply alcohol from qualifying premises in Wales, or to authorise that, at a selling price below the minimum (Public Health (Minimum Price for Alcohol) (Wales) Act 2018, s.2; minimum unit price in reg 2 of the Minimum Unit Price (Wales) Regulations 2019, as amended). It binds the seller; it limits how cheaply a drink can be sold, not what a visitor may drink.
laws.heading: Public Health (Minimum Price for Alcohol) (Wales) Act 2018, s.2; SI 2019/1472, reg 2

laws.rule: Wales bans the supply of listed single-use plastic products to consumers in Wales, including by delivery to a Welsh address (Environmental Protection (Single-use Plastic Products) (Wales) Act 2023, ss.2 and 5; in force 30 October 2023). The Act's schedule lists the products. It includes straws, plates, takeaway food containers made of expanded or foamed polystyrene, balloon sticks, most carrier bags, cotton buds and any product made of oxo-degradable plastic, each with its own exemptions (for example straws for health or disability reasons). The offence is committed by the supplier and is punishable by a fine (s.6); a visitor is affected mainly by finding these items unavailable.
laws.heading: Environmental Protection (Single-use Plastic Products) (Wales) Act 2023, ss.1, 2, 5, 6 and schedule

laws.rule: In Wales an enclosed vehicle is smoke-free when it is used for social, domestic or other private purposes, more than one person is present and one of them is a child, meaning a person under 18 (Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020, reg 15(3)(b)). Local authorities enforce it. The fixed penalty for the child-in-vehicle offence is GBP 100 (about A$190 at RBA 30 Oct 2026), or GBP 75 (about A$143) at the discounted amount (regs 20 and 21).
laws.heading: Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020, regs 15, 20, 21

laws.rule: Since 1 June 2025 it is an offence in Wales to supply, offer to supply or hold for supply a single-use vape (a vape not designed to be reused, such as one that cannot be refilled or recharged). The offence is aimed at shops and other suppliers, not at a visitor using a vape. The regulations apply in Wales only and give officers powers of entry and civil sanctions (regs 8 to 10).
laws.heading: Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) (Wales) Regulations 2024 (WSI 2024/1324), regs 1, 3 and 4

laws.rule: In England and Wales a person may not use an adult firework between 11 pm and 7 am, except on four nights: the first day of Chinese New Year, Diwali and 31 December (until 1 am the next morning) and 5 November (until midnight) (Fireworks Regulations 2004, reg 7). A person under 18 may not possess an adult firework in a public place (reg 4).
laws.heading: Fireworks Regulations 2004, regs 4 and 7 (England and Wales)

laws.rule: Wales shares the England limit for drink-driving: 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 ml of breath, 80 mg per 100 ml of blood or 107 mg per 100 ml of urine (Road Traffic Act 1988, s.11(2)). Scotland's limit is lower (50 mg per 100 ml of blood).
laws.heading: Road Traffic Act 1988, s.11(2)
